title: Port Knocking
desc: fwknop-compatible Single Packet Authorization (SPA): the client sends one encrypted, replay-protected knock packet, and only after it is authenticated are ports such as SSH opened for that address for a limited time. Ports can be blocked in the system firewall, or Port Forwarding, Protocol Routing and STUN can open them based on the knock.

status.title: Status
status.listenError: Failed to listen on the knock port: {err}
status.udpOff: Not listening on UDP; only knocks relayed by Protocol Routing are received
status.fwNotNeeded: No rule has firewall blocking turned on

os.title: Firewall blocking is not supported on this system
os.hint: Firewall blocking needs nftables or iptables + ipset on Linux. Knock requirements for Port Forwarding, Protocol Routing and STUN do not depend on the firewall and work as usual.

missing.title: nft or iptables + ipset not found
missing.hint: Install nftables (recommended) or iptables and ipset, then save the settings to retry.

permission.title: No permission to modify the firewall
permission.hint: Gately must run as root; with Docker, use host networking and add cap_add: NET_ADMIN.

unsupported.title: The kernel has no nf_tables and no usable iptables + ipset
unsupported.hint: On Synology and similar systems, use the official Gately Docker image (it bundles iptables and ipset).

error.title: Failed to write firewall rules
error.hint: Gately retries every minute. See the error below and the runtime log for details.

grants.title: Active grants ({count})
grants.empty: No address has knocked successfully and is still within its access duration
grants.gatelyOnly: Only for Port Forwarding, Protocol Routing and STUN
grants.revokeConfirm: After revoking, this address has to knock again. Established connections are not affected. Revoke it?

rule.portsHelp: Ports a client may ask to open, such as tcp/22 or udp/51820, separated by commas. A bare port number means TCP. Every port in the client's -A option must be in this list.
rule.firewallHelp: When on, these ports are blocked in the system firewall and only addresses that knocked successfully are let through, which protects services such as this host's sshd (Linux only). When off, the firewall is left alone and the rule only serves "Require knock" in Port Forwarding, Protocol Routing and STUN.
rule.firewallWarn: Before turning this on, make sure you can still log in to this host from the LAN (knock-exempt by default in the global settings) or another way: if Gately is killed, the blocking rules stay until Gately starts again. Established connections are not affected.
rule.keysHelp: base64 encoded, matching fwknop's KEY_BASE64 and HMAC_KEY_BASE64. You can enter keys generated by fwknop -k. After changing the keys, old clients can no longer knock.
rule.timeoutHelp: After a successful knock, new connections can be made during this time. Established connections stay up after it expires.
rule.timeoutWithMax: {n} s (clients may request up to {max} s)
rule.maxTimeoutHelp: Upper limit when a client asks for a longer duration with -f; 0 ignores the duration the client requests. A request shorter than the access duration is always honored.
rule.userHelp: Only accept knocks whose packet carries this username. fwknop sends the local login name by default; use -U to set it.
rule.requireAddrHelp: Reject knocks without an address (fwknop -s). The client must state the address to open with -R or -a, so a packet intercepted in transit cannot be replayed first from another address.

settings.title: Port Knocking settings
settings.portHelp: UDP port that receives knock packets; the fwknop client defaults to 62201. Enter 0 to skip UDP and only receive knocks sent through a Protocol Routing TCP port (fwknop -P tcp).
settings.autoFirewallHelp: Opens the knock port in the system firewall (OpenWrt fw4, firewalld, ufw, etc.). Once firewall blocking is active it also opens the protected ports, so access is decided only by knocking.
settings.allowLanHelp: LAN, Tailscale (100.64.0.0/10), link-local addresses and this host's IPv6 /64 can reach protected ports without knocking, so you do not lock yourself out. Affects firewall blocking only.
settings.allowListHelp: IPs or ranges that can reach protected ports without knocking, one per line. Affects firewall blocking only.
settings.maxAgeHelp: Maximum difference between the packet timestamp and this host's time; anything beyond it is treated as expired or replayed. The clocks of both client and server must be accurate.

client.title: fwknop client configuration: {name}
client.tcpHelp: Listening port of the Protocol Routing rule, which needs a "Port Knocking" route
client.udpOff: The UDP knock port is not enabled in the global settings. Use Protocol Routing or set the port first

addrHelp.resolve: -R: the client looks up its own public IPv4 and writes it into the packet, so an intercepted packet is useless for another address.
addrHelp.source: -s: opens the address the packet comes from. Suited to networks where looking up the public IP is inconvenient.
addrHelp.fixed: -a: opens the given address, for example to knock for another device.

client.rcHelp: After saving it to ~/.fwknoprc, run fwknop -n {name} to knock.
client.install: fwknop client: brew install fwknop on macOS, apt install fwknop-client on Debian / Ubuntu, or install it in WSL on Windows. The fwknop client can only send knock packets over IPv4, so the server address must be reachable over IPv4. The command and config contain keys, so keep them safe.
